n: In December 1831, former member Ezra Booth was publishing hostile letters in an Ohio newspaper. The Lord tells Joseph and Sidney to pause the Bible translation and preach, explaining the gospel from the scriptures as the Spirit gives power.

f.w: expounding the mysteries thereof out of the scriptures

n: They should preach in the surrounding regions and in the Church for a season, until told otherwise.

f.w: for the space of a season

n: This is a temporary mission. They returned to translating about a month later (D&C 73).
Work in the vineyard, testify, and prepare the way for revelations still to come.
Whoever reads this should understand and accept it.
Those who receive will be given more—even power.

f.w: unto him that receiveth it shall be given more abundantly

n: Confront critics openly; invite them to discuss publicly or privately. Faithfulness will expose their shame. The Lord answers criticism with truth, not silence.

f.g: Confound = refute, leave without an answer.

n: Let opponents bring their strongest arguments against the Lord.
A precious promise from Isaiah: no weapon formed against them will prosper.

f.w: no weapon that is formed against you shall prosper

n: Anyone who speaks against them will be confounded in God’s timing.
Keep the commandments, which are true and faithful.
